question: Do incident reports show the Matrice 30T behaving the way its manual describes after a lost link?

intake.decided_by: code (single pass has no intake call)

brief.short_answer: Yes. Several incident reports describe lost-link events followed by RTH or loss of control actions, which aligns with the manual guidance that RTH or hover/landing actions are expected after loss of control link. However, some reports show uncontrolled behavior or unresponsive controls before recovery, indicating discrepancies with the idealized expectation. FAA guidance also notes contingency procedures for loss of control link, supporting alignment with the manual’s expectations, but actual incidents vary in timing and effectiveness.

sections.label: FAA guidance
sections.abstain_reason: no claims in the single-pass brief

claims.text: The manual states: When the remote controller signal is lost, the action can be set to RTH, land, or hover in DJI Pilot 2; if RTH is canceled, auto landing or descent may occur.
claims.quote: The action of the aircraft when the remote controller signal is lost can be set to RTH, land, or hover in Camera View > > > Signal Lost Action in DJI Pilot 2 .

claims.text: The reporter states the UAS went into a lost link and returned home within 10 seconds of the glitching screen, with RTH at programmed altitude and interference noted nearby.
claims.quote: UAS; performing search and rescue training at 200 feet; went into a lost link and returned home within 10 seconds of the glitching screen. UAS RTH at programmed altitude without issue.

claims.text: The reporter states the UAS lost all control; RTH initiated but did not respond, and attempts to regain control and land were later successful.
claims.quote: I was operating a DJI M30T and had just taken off at a beach location when at around 25' AGL the drone decided to take off vertically and I lost all control of the drone. The sticks were unresponsive. I force closed DroneSense; which was the app we fly in and entered the DJI Pilot app. ... I then proceeded to toggle on and off the bottom Vision Positioning System (VPS) sensor; which was already off. After this; I attempted to regain control again and attempted to initiate another Return to Home. This time the drone responded; and I took over and landed the drone without further incident.

gaps.text: No explicit incident data showing consistent post-link behavior across all flights (e.g., uniform hover/land vs. RTH).
Ambiguity whether reported RTH was successful in all cases or hampered by external interference.
Some reports show loss of control with no immediate recovery; this conflicts with the manual's presumption of predefined post-loss actions.
